notes: The physical mesh is row-major with 9 rows and 6 columns.
The analytical network lists dimensions as columns then rows.
D2D latency is modeled as a per-hop adjacent-link latency. It is independent of the on-die noc-width-bits.
The remote-memory pool is attached to every physical mesh-boundary NPU.
The 512 GB/s remote-memory bandwidth and 100 ns latency are shared simulator assumptions.
The capacity profile describes local HBM placement per NPU.

User-authorized engineering comparison point (2026-10-16): 10 x 10 Core grid on a 25 mm x 32 mm compute Die (800 mm2), 0.75 MiB SRAM/Core and 512-bit NoC. Architectural PE peak is 126.6 INT4 TOPS, numerically compared with the TX8 128 BF16 TFLOPS reference; precision and independent measurement are not equivalent. Vec FP32-equivalent peak is 12.65728 T eq-op/s, not the TX8 1 T reference. Legacy HBM remains the preserved 4 x 16 GB / 410 GB/s per-stack reference (64 GB and 1640 GB/s), not current DOCX HBM3E.

Factory compute default (phase 2, 2026-10-18): the coarse-die node (coarse_die_v2 typed descriptor, materialized verbatim into resolved_die_model.json) replaces the legacy die node as the checked-in backend; die (mesh_die_v1) and compute.peak-perf-tflops remain supported as mutually exclusive alternatives and their aligned capacity profiles are kept for explicit fixtures.
